title: How can one rule give {{NAME_6}}'s age from {{NAME_5}}'s age?
description: {{NAME_6}} is three years younger than {{NAME_5}}. A rule with letters gives the younger age from the older age, and it is used when {{NAME_5}} is twenty. Keeko doubts that the rule adds three.
teaching_notes: One idea: when one person is younger, the rule takes away from the older age, and the same letter rule fits every age. Watch for students who add three because the words say three years.

source: {{NAME_5}} is 3 years older than {{NAME_6}}. Write an expression for {{NAME_6}}'s age using s for {{NAME_5}}'s age
video_script.why: A learner sees that the same two people give a second rule, this time by taking away three from the older age.
video_script.substitution: The book's own question about {{NAME_5}} and {{NAME_6}}, now asked the other way round, with the age twenty.
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_5}} and {{NAME_6}}, whose ages are always three years apart
video_script.wrong_answer: the younger age is s plus three
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds three to the older age because the question says three years, but the younger person has the smaller age; with s as ten the sum gives thirteen, which is older.

final_answer.spoken: the rule is eigh equals s minus three, and {{NAME_6}} is seventeen years old

never_show: the age 17 before the answer beat
maths_rules: {{NAME_6}} is 3 years younger, so the age of {{NAME_6}} is 3 less than the age of {{NAME_5}}.
With s for the age of {{NAME_5}} and a for the age of {{NAME_6}}: a = s - 3.
video_script.design: One idea: younger means less, so subtract. Assumes the idea of a letter standing for an age. The two names stay on the stage and the arrow between the ages is reversed. Wrong idea: add three to the older age.

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>{{NAME_6}} is three years younger than {{NAME_5}}, and the book wants a rule for the age of {{NAME_6}}.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>The rule must start from the age of {{NAME_5}}, whatever that age may be.
How can we write such a rule?

<bookmark mark='gv2'/>Let s stand for the age of {{NAME_5}}, and eigh for the age of {{NAME_6}}.

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Three less than s is written s minus three.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>The rule is eigh equals s minus three, for every age of {{NAME_5}}.

<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Then eigh equals twenty minus three.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a = s − 3, and a = 17 years

marks.ans: 17 years is boxed beside the rule

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>{{NAME_6}} is seventeen years old when {{NAME_5}} is twenty.
The rule for every age is eigh equals s minus three.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: the younger age is s + 3, struck out; the two bars come back with s as 10 and the sum 13 drawn longer than the older bar

marks.d2: the two bars come back with the older bar at ten

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Keeko thinks the younger age is s plus three, since the question says three years.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>Try s as ten, and that rule gives thirteen for the younger one.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>That is more than the older age, so the rule must take three away, not add it.
